correctness.rationale: For 0<a<1, the adjoint action on normalized monomials follows by taking coefficients in the reproducing-kernel identity; summing their squared image norms by Tonelli gives the finite Gaussian integral exp(|(1−a)u|²/(1−a²))/(1−a²). Equivalently this defines the bounded compact extension via the adjoint matrix. The Taylor series about u diagonalizes the action coefficient by coefficient, identifies all nonzero eigenvalues by compactness, and rules out Jordan chains by injectivity of the coefficient at the claimed eigenvalue on its eigenline. With v_n=(z−u)^n/√n! and w_n=z^n exp(conj(u)z)/√n!, the bounded rank-one projection is f↦⟨f,w_n⟩v_n, since the normalized jets pair to δ_mn and commute with the operator. Gaussian orthogonality gives ∥v_n∥²=L_n(−|u|²); completion of the Gaussian square gives ∥w_n∥²=exp(|u|²)∥v_n∥². Mityagin–Siegl–Viola independently support the fixed-displacement prefactor by the adapted parameter below. In the frozen proof, the Bessel weights with λ=√n|u| concentrate at j/λ→1 by the consecutive quotient λ²/(j+1)² (geometric tails outside each fixed relative neighborhood); the falling-factorial multiplier tends in probability to exp(−|u|²/2) and lies in [0,1]. The stated Bessel integral gives the prefactor. For n|u_n|²→τ² the finite Laguerre series is dominated termwise by C^j/(j!)² and converges to I_0(2τ), including τ=0. Complete minimality follows from polynomial spans and the bounded jets. All enumerations have these same individual coordinate projections if they are Schauder bases; coordinate projections would then be uniformly bounded as differences of consecutive partial sum projections. Similarity to a normal or scalar-type spectral operator likewise implies bounded spectral projections. At u=0 the normalized monomials are orthonormal.

evidence: MSV Eqs. (2.13)–(2.18) use right and left Hermite functions h_n(x+ib), h_n(x−ib) as biorthogonal pairs, with b real and nonzero. For the Fock pair first rotate u to r=|u|. Let W_t f(z)=exp(tz−t²/2) f(z−t) for real t, Rf(z)=f(iz), and U=R W_{r/2}^{−1}. Under the usual Bargmann transform B taking h_n to z^n/√n!, B[h_n(·+δ)](z)=exp(−δz/√2−δ²/4)(z+δ/√2)^n/√n!, from the Gaussian ground state and creation operator (or the Hermite generating function). Direct substitution gives Uv_n=i^n exp(−r²/4)B[h_n(·+ib)] and Uw_n=i^n exp(r²/4)B[h_n(·−ib)], with b=r/√2. The factors cancel in the rank-one projection.
The prior Fock record's trace-norm series writes these exact rank-one terms via the same shifted polynomials and derivative kernels.

The resultary projection terms are already the eigenline Taylor-jet projections, since they commute and act as identity on the corresponding shifted monomial and zero on the others.

originality.rationale: There is demonstrable prior coverage, not merely a similar title. A published Fock-jet result contains the identical rank-one terms and both norm identities in its proof, for more general complex slopes. In a separate prior formulation, the whole family of projections is unitarily equivalent to the imaginary-shift oscillator projections of Mityagin–Siegl–Viola. Their exact Laguerre formula and sharp growth (with an error term) transfer with |u|=√2 times their shift parameter. The asserted crossover is the classical compact-uniform Mehler–Heine limit; the basis and similarity consequences follow mechanically. There is no distinct substantial remainder in this record.
